name: Nguluwan
region: Ngulu Atoll, Yap State; also Guror village, Gilman', Yap
orthography_note: IPA, from Sakiyama's transcription (pp. 107-108), which differs from the official Yapese spelling in the long vowels (ëë for ea, ää for ae, öö for oe): ch = t͡ʃ, j = d͡ʒ, th = θ, ng = ŋ, y = j; ë [æ], ä [ɐ], ö [œ], a [ɑ]; doubled letters for long vowels (decision sakiyama1982-symbols).
notes: Spoken by 28 people on Ngulu Atoll and by some in Guror, Gilman', which holds Ngulu in a soway relationship (Sakiyama 1982: 105). 'Neither Yapese nor Ulithian in the strict sense of the word, although we can define it as a quite peculiar dialect among Yapese', with Ulithian loans and calques in the lexicon and in possessive constructions (pp. 106, 113); entered as a dialect of Yapese (decision sakiyama1982-nguluwan). Glottolog 5.4 has Nguluwan as a language beside Yapese in Yapic (yape1250). Sakiyama compares it with Yapese (§1.3, pp. 108-111): Nguluwan lacks all of Yapese's glottalized consonants and its glottal stop q; Yapese -iq is -iy, -oq is -wwa, medial q is w or y (naqun : nawun 'house', raqay : rayay 'hundred'); Yapese bVqV-, mVqV- are bwV-, mwV-; Yapese d and th merge as th; words begin with glides y-, w- where Yapese has a vowel (arow : yaraw 'land'); vowel correspondences are not regular. 'Such innovations are much indebted to Ulithian influence' (p. 111). No correspondence rows: the lect is shown by its sourced inventory. Coordinates from Glottolog.
